units.source_text: 说不定老师从我手里接过两条切斯特菲尔德香烟的时候，早已着穿了呢？

en.t: Perhaps, when the teacher took the two cartons of Chesterfield cigarettes from my hands, he had already seen through me?

units.source_text: 他之所以不问，也许只是为了从远处忍耐地等待着我自觉的忏悔吧。

en.t: Perhaps the reason he did not ask was simply that he was patiently waiting from a distance for me to confess of my own accord.

units.source_text: 也许还以升大学为诱饵，换取了我的仔海，

en.t: Perhaps he had even used advancement to university as bait in order to draw out my confession,

units.source_text: 假如我不忏悔，就不让我升学，以惩罚我不老实；

en.t: and if I did not confess, he would refuse to let me go on to higher studies, punishing me for my dishonesty;

units.source_text: 假如仔海，就盘查悔改的效验，尔后施以格外的恩典，允许我升大学。

en.t: but if I did confess, he would examine the sincerity of my repentance and then grant me the special favor of allowing me to enter university.

units.source_text: 而且，更大典圈套是老师命令副司不告诉我这件事。

en.t: Moreover, the greater trap was that the teacher had ordered the deputy priest not to tell me about it.

units.source_text: 倘使我真是无辜，那么我可以无所感觉，无所知晓地度日子。

en.t: If I were truly innocent, then I could pass my days feeling nothing and knowing nothing.

units.source_text: 另一方面，倘使我犯了罪，并且多少还有点智慧，那么我可以完全模仿无辜，度过纯洁的沉默的日子。

en.t: On the other hand, if I had committed a sin and still possessed even a little wisdom, then I could imitate innocence perfectly and spend pure, silent days.

units.source_text: 就是说，反过没有必要忏悔的日子。

en.t: In other words, by turning things around, they would be days in which there was no need to confess.
Even imitation would be good enough.
This was the most prudent method.

units.source_text: 这是证明我心地纯洁的惟一的道路。

en.t: This was the only path by which I could prove the purity of my heart.

units.source_text: 老师就是这样暗示了这一点。

en.t: That was exactly what the teacher had hinted to me.

units.source_text: 他让我落入这个圈套……一想到这里，我便义愤填膺。

en.t: He had made me fall into this trap... and the moment I thought of that, I was filled with righteous indignation.
